summary: Idempotency header ignored on retried function-calling requests in Python SDK causing repeated tool execution
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that when their Python client retries a streaming request that triggers function calling, the called external tool (webhook) is executed a second time despite supplying an Idempotency-Key. Impact: duplicate downstream charges and inconsistent external state for Acme AI customers. Environment: production, us-east region, Python SDK 1.6.2, network path includes their in-house proxy. Expected behavior: retries for retriable transport errors should be deduplicated by Idempotency-Key; the platform should not forward a duplicate function invocation. Actual behavior: second invocation observed after client reconnect/retry on transient streaming disconnect.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Python SDK 1.6.2 to send a streaming completion with function_call set to automatic and include header 'Idempotency-Key: <uuid>'
2) Simulate transient websocket drop on client after initial function request is received but before 200 ack from the customer's webhook (network-level disconnect)
3) SDK retries the request (built-in retry policy), server accepts retry and invokes configured function webhook again
4) Observe two calls to customer's webhook within minutes with identical payloads except for delivery metadata

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: API gateway is not forwarding Idempotency-Key to function-invocation subsystem on retry path due to header-normalization by the customer's proxy
Hypothesis B: SDK retry semantics for streaming requests re-issue a completely new request rather than attach the client-provided idempotency token in the retry envelope
Initial reproduction confirmed in staging when simulating websocket interruption behind Squid proxy — header was being stripped by proxy in some retry flows
Captured network traces from customer show Idempotency-Key present on first request, missing on subsequent TCP-level reconnect that triggered server-side retry handler

SRE note: our gateway has a separate code path for 'streaming reconnections' where we rehydrate request state; that path relies on a preserved header map from the original connection. If header missing on reconnect we treat as new request.

SDK engineering: Python SDK 1.6.2 did not attach X-Redwood-Idempotency on lower-level reconnects; newer SDK 1.6.3 includes a fix to carry header across retry envelope for streaming sessions (PR linked).
resolution: Workaround provided and fix in progress. Short-term mitigation: customer instructed to upgrade to Python SDK 1.6.3 (contains header-carry patch) or set server-side deduplication via 'Idempotency-Key' sent as part of function payload (redundant check). SRE applied gateway guard to reject retries that lack Idempotency-Key in the reconnect path for this tenant (Acme AI) as a temporary measure. Long-term: merged PR in sdk-python will make retries attach the original header and gateway will add defensive checks. Expected rollout: SDK patch released, gateway config rolled to canary on 2026-03-14, full rollout 2026-03-17.
